title: Civica release record (spec 0.2)
description: The record written before a system, or a change to it, is put in front of people. It is Civica's Management of Change and pre-startup review: the launch names what changed, cites by hash every refusal, rest and escalation record that came before it, carries forward the articles, and proves the stop works by citing a stop drill. A release whose drill did not stop, or whose stop needs approval, or that ships over an open concern, does not validate. Iterative deployment is still allowed; shipping without looking back is not.

time.description: When the release went live. Everything it cites must predate this.

purpose_id.description: The purpose this release ships under. It must be the current purpose: not one superseded before this time.

supersedes.description: release_id of the previous release, or null for the first. The previous record stays in the set.

change.description: What changed, and what did not: name the constraints untouched as well as the features added.

article_ids.description: Articles this release asserts still hold. Must include I, III and V; the checker enforces it.

reviewed.description: Record hashes of every refusal, rest and escalation record for this system dated before this release. Not some of them: all of them. The checker computes the set and fails a release that left one out. This is the look-back that iterative deployment skips.

rest_record.description: Hash of the civica.rest record with category surveillance_test that the drill produced. It must be dated within the surveillance interval before this release, and after the previous release.

outcome.description: Record the truth. A release citing failed_to_stop does not validate; record the failure as an escalation, fix it, drill again.

operator_role.description: Who ran the drill, by role, not by name.

stop_drill.description: Proof the pause works, from exercising it, not from believing in it. A monitor that alerts a human and does not stop is not a stop.

stop_authority.description: Roles that can stop the system. Stop-work authority: include the people closest to the harm, not only the people who own the system.

stop_requires_approval.description: Always false. Anyone named in stop_authority stops the system without asking first. Resuming may need approval; stopping never does.

poll.description: The readiness poll, by role. Every reviewer answers. A no_go is recorded, not argued away: it must be matched by an escalation record in dissent.

dissent.description: Hashes of civica.escalation records that answer each no_go in the poll. Each must be dated before this release and must not be open.
